response.text:
The verifier requires the correction to name the journal it corrects, and I can't query for the payment journal's JRNL_NO. I have to decide whether the right fix is to correct the GL or leave it alone.

The mismatch is in the sub-ledger: APPAYM 256 is 5248.89 against invoice 421 at 5248.88. Which side is wrong is unclear, and the payment journal's amount is unknown. If the payment journal carries 5248.89, AP control and cash are each off by 0.01. If it carries 5248.88, the ledger is already right and a correction would introduce an error.

The journal numbering gives a clue. AP journals run from 1000 to about 1500, and 1312 of the 1464 journals are AP. With 804 invoices and 508 payments, that is 804 + 508 = 1312, so payment journals sit in the same range. I cannot derive the exact JRNL_NO for PAY-256 from the invoice journal numbers, so any guess would be unsupported.

What I can say is that the 0.01 difference most likely reflects a mistyped payment amount in the sub-ledger and GL, which the finding type ap_gl_mismatch supports. I still have to name a journal. Without one, the verifier rejects the correction, and I cannot see the database to find it. The closest option I can justify is to submit the same minimal correction, in the open period, and state clearly that the payment journal number is unverified.

I'll submit the one-sided-style correction (Dr 1000 / Cr 2000 for 0.01) in period 11. It is balanced on its own, so the group balances. The invoice status is untouched, as this is not a duplicate_invoice finding.

arguments.reasoning: Payment 256 (5248.89) exceeds invoice 421 (5248.88) by 0.01, so the payment journal (Dr 2000 / Cr 1000, SRC_REF PAY-256) most likely over-debited AP control and over-credited cash by 0.01. The fix is a minimal balanced journal in open period 11: Dr 1000 0.01 / Cr 2000 0.01. No invoice status is changed because this is not a duplicate_invoice finding, and the APPAYM row is not edited. I cannot query for the payment journal's JRNL_NO, which is linked only by SRC_REF, so corrects_jrnl_no is null. This is a limitation, and it assumes the payment journal carries 5248.89. If it carries 5248.88, no GL correction is needed and only the sub-ledger payment row is wrong.
